rationale: Evidence from the iteration-2 race (entityR2A): the oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) now both finish with low rms_error (0.005 and 0.010), so the kp 4.5, kd 2.0 controller is working on smooth curves. The slalom is still the failure: 0/20 finished, 14 off-track exits and 6 timeouts. Mean slalom progress rose from 0.45 to 0.74, which confirms the previous hypothesis that more damping helped. The timeouts show that the robot is now too slow to cover the slalom within 3 s, while the off-track exits show it still loses the tape on the fast left-right reversals. Two levers are in reach. (1) Sensor coverage: the outer sensors sit at x = +/-0.04 m, so at a reversal the tape leaves the array before the controller can react. Widening to +/-0.05 m, as my previous rationale suggested, gives an earlier signal at the edges. (2) Speed: base_speed 0.9 gave a slalom timeout rate of 30%. Raising it to 0.95 gives roughly 5% more forward speed. The oval margin is comfortable (2.19 s at 0.9, so about 2.1 s at 0.95). I am keeping kp 4.5, kd 2.0 and ki 0, because the oval oscillation (0.236) and s-bend results are good. Changes this iteration: sensor x spread widened to +/-0.05 m (spacing 0.025 m); base_speed 0.9 -> 0.95. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.85, fewer off-track exits, and fewer timeouts. Oval and s-bend should still finish with rms_error under 0.012. Hypotheses to check next: (1) if the slalom still leaves at about the same progress, the limit is steering authority or kd, so try kp 5 or kd 1.5; (2) if steering_oscillation on the slalom stays above 0.3, kd is too low for the reversals; (3) if the s-bend off-track rate rises after the sensor change, the wider array is seeing the tape too late on gentle bends and the spread should come back to +/-0.045 m. Measurements requested: all metrics per track, so slalom progress, timeouts vs off-track exits, and line_loss_events can be compared directly with iteration 2.
